title: Perfect pushforward and restriction for supported open immersions
statement: Let j:(U, O_U) \to (X, O_X) be an open immersion of ringed spaces [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], and let T be a closed subset of X contained in U. For a complex, cohomology supported on T means that every cohomology sheaf restricts to zero on X minus T. If F is a perfect object of D(O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] whose cohomology sheaves are supported on T, then Rj_*F is perfect on X [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Moreover, for every E in D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] whose cohomology sheaves are supported on T, the canonical map E \to Rj_*(E restricted to U) is an isomorphism, and for every such F the canonical map j_!F \to Rj_*F is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put V=X\setminus T, open since T is closed, and W=U\cap V; since T\subseteq U, X=U\cup V is an open cover. Let G be an object of D(O_U) whose cohomology sheaves are supported on T, so G|_W has zero cohomology sheaves and G|_W=0. By [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] applied to j and the open V (with j^{-1}(V)=W), (Rj_*G)|_V is canonically R(j|_W)_*(G|_W)=0; applied to j and the open U (with j^{-1}(U)=U and induced map the identity), (Rj_*G)|_U is canonically G, and under this identification the restriction to U of the unit of j^{-1}\dashv Rj_* is the identity. Now let E be in D(O_X) with cohomology sheaves supported on T and take G=E|_U, which is again supported on T. The canonical map E\to Rj_*(E|_U) restricts on U to the identity of E|_U, and on V it is a map between objects with zero cohomology sheaves (E|_V=0 by the support hypothesis, (Rj_*(E|_U))|_V=0 by the above). Hence its cone has cohomology sheaves vanishing on U and on V, so zero cohomology sheaves, so the cone is zero and the map is an isomorphism (an isomorphism of objects is detected on cohomology sheaves, which are local).

Let F be in D(O_U) with cohomology sheaves supported on T. Extension by zero j_! on modules is exact and left adjoint to restriction [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact], so j_!F is computed termwise on any representing complex and j_! commutes with taking cohomology sheaves. Immediately from the construction of extension by zero (Stacks, proof of 08DF), (j_!F)|_U=F and (j_!F)|_V=j_{W!}(F|_W)=0, since F|_W=0 by the support hypothesis. By the preceding step (with G=F), also (Rj_*F)|_U=F and (Rj_*F)|_V=0, and the canonical map j_!F\to Rj_*F restricts on U to the identity of F. So it is an isomorphism on each member of the cover {U,V}, and the cone argument of the preceding step shows it is an isomorphism.

Perfectness is local: by [def-pc-perfect-complex] an object is perfect when it is, on the members of some open cover, isomorphic to strictly perfect complexes, and covers of the members of a cover combine. Let F be a perfect object of D(O_U) with cohomology sheaves supported on T. On the cover {U,V} of the first step, (Rj_*F)|_U=F is perfect, and (Rj_*F)|_V=0 by the first step, and the zero complex is strictly perfect. Hence Rj_*F is perfect on X.
